title: Hardware Troubleshooting Detective
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Solve broken-robot cases by choosing which of the six hardware checks to run, reading the clues, and naming the hidden fault with as few checks as possible.

educational.topic: Systematic hardware fault isolation on a robot
learningObjectives: Analyze a robot symptom to list the most likely hardware faults
Select the troubleshooting check that best separates the suspects
Interpret partial evidence (clues) that points toward a fault
Justify which check to run first based on speed and how much it rules out
prerequisites: The six-item hardware troubleshooting checklist (Chapter 2: Hardware Troubleshooting)
Changing one thing at a time while debugging (Chapter 1: A Strategy for Hard Problems)

controls.label: Is it powered?
controls.purpose: Inspect the USB cable and power LED

controls.purpose: Inspect the files on the board

options: USB cable not plugged in all the way

controls.label: New broken robot
controls.purpose: Start a new case with a different fault

simulationModel.modelType: Hidden-fault diagnostic game with scored evidence gathering
assumptions: Exactly one fault is active per robot
Each check reports fine, a clue, or the fault itself
limitations: Real robots can have more than one fault at a time
Six faults cover common beginner problems, not every possible failure

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Case-based diagnostic reasoning with cost feedback
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Choose checks, interpret colored rings and log results, submit a hypothesis
keyQuestions: Which faults could cause this symptom?
Which check separates those suspects fastest?
What does an amber clue tell you even though it is not the fault?
If the motors do not spin at all, which check do you run first and why?
commonMisconceptions: Running every check in list order is the best strategy
If the code has no errors, the problem cannot be in the program
A wire that looks connected must be fully seated
assessmentOpportunities: Recorder sheets listing symptom, check order, and result
Three solved cases in a row with a score of 60 or more
Written justification of the first check for a new symptom
